title: Governed Material Descriptions and Material Keynotes for Revit
license_confirmation: I wrote this or have the right to share it, and I agree to publish it under CC BY 4.0 (text/JSON) and MIT (code).

context.tool_or_bridge: ZEN material CSV workflow; applicable to a Revit Bridge / ExternalEvent workflow

intent: Normalize Revit Material Description and Keynote data so an AI agent can improve incomplete material metadata without inventing unsupported technical information, while preserving deterministic Revit round-trip behavior and producing keynote values suitable for material tags and sheet legends.
use_when: A Revit material schedule contains blank, incomplete or contradictory Description values.
Materials need Keynote values for material tags or sheet keynote legends.
Material data is exported to CSV, AI-reviewed and read back into Revit.
A Revit Bridge reads material properties, requests an AI proposal, previews the proposal and commits approved changes.
not_for: Inventing manufacturer, product, grade, performance or specification properties that are not supported by the source data.
Replacing an approved office or project keynote database without explicit authorization.
Treating appearance assets as authoritative physical specifications.
Automatically describing analytical, phase, poche, default or other graphic/system materials as construction materials unless the user explicitly wants them documented.

iterations.instruction: Export Revit materials and use AI to fill missing or inconsistent material descriptions from Name, Class, existing Description and appearance data.
iterations.result: AI produced normalized descriptions for physical materials and corrected several contradictions.
iterations.problem: The first description grammar also carried dimensions from material names into Description, for example panel and tile sizes.
iterations.found_by: Human review of the edited material schedule in Excel showed that dimensions made the Description less reusable and duplicated type/name information.

iterations.result: Description was redefined as a dimension-free human-readable identity: base material, product/form, finish/treatment, color, pattern/texture, and supported grade/performance terms.
iterations.problem: Appearance data can contain plausible but non-authoritative product information, and existing descriptions can conflict with Name or appearance.
iterations.found_by: Examples showed conflicting colors and finishes between material Name, Description and Appearance Asset.

iterations.instruction: Create logic for assigning Material Keynotes used by Revit tags and legends.
iterations.result: Keynote was separated from Description: Description identifies the material variant; Keynote is the documentation identity. Existing keys remain authoritative. A new local suffix system may be generated only when the user explicitly requests creation of a new project keynote set.
iterations.problem: The alphabetic suffix after a classification section is not inherently an official semantic code and must not be treated as one without an authoritative keynote table.
iterations.found_by: Existing material schedules contained repeated section-based keys with local suffixes that did not expose a universal letter meaning.

final_rule.lesson: Separate the four identities of a Revit material: Name is the BIM identifier, Description is the human-readable material identity, Keynote is the documentation/tagging identity, and Appearance is the visual identity. AI may interpret incomplete evidence, but deterministic rules control what is written back to Revit.
final_rule.rule:
1. PRESERVE THE ROUND-TRIP SCHEMA
When editing an exported material CSV intended for Revit re-import, do not add, remove, rename or reorder columns. Do not rename materials. Only modify fields explicitly authorized by the workflow, normally Description and/or Keynote.

2. CLASSIFY BEFORE ENRICHING
First decide whether the row represents a physical/documented material or a Revit system/graphic/analytical placeholder. Do not invent construction descriptions or classification keynotes for system-only rows unless a separate internal namespace is explicitly requested.

3. MATERIAL DESCRIPTION GRAMMAR
Generate Description from supported evidence in this order:
Base Material -> Product/Form -> Finish/Treatment -> Color -> Pattern/Texture -> Grade/Performance.
Omit any component that is not supported.

Description describes what the material is and how it is finished. It does not describe its instance size or type dimensions.

Hard exclusions from Description:
- dimensions, thicknesses and sizes;
- model/type numbers unless they are part of the actual product identity explicitly required by the user;
- project codes;
- keynote numbers;
- unsupported manufacturer/product claims.

4. EVIDENCE AUTHORITY
Use Name and Class primarily for material identity.
Use an existing Description as evidence, but test it for contradictions.
Use explicit terms in Name as strong evidence.
Use Appearance Asset and appearance properties for visual attributes such as color, gloss, texture and transparency.
Do not promote an appearance texture or asset name into a physical/specification claim unless corroborated.
Use Keynote only as a classification hint, not as proof of physical properties.

5. CONFLICT HANDLING
If Name, Description, Class and Appearance conflict, do not silently merge contradictory claims. Prefer explicit material identity over purely visual appearance. Produce a proposal for review when the conflict could change specification meaning. A directly committed correction is acceptable only when the contradiction is unambiguous and the governing workflow allows it.

6. KEYNOTE AUTHORITY
If an approved office/project keynote table exists:
- preserve existing valid keynotes unless remapping is explicitly authorized;
- select only keys that exist in that table;
- never invent a new key because a classification number merely looks plausible;
- if no reliable match exists, leave the field blank or request review.

Match priority:
a. exact approved material/library match;
b. equivalent approved material family;
c. approved keynote database/table match;
d. approved specification/classification mapping;
e. no match -> review/blank.

7. GENERATING A NEW PROJECT KEYNOTE SET
Only generate new material keynotes when the user explicitly requests creation of a new project keynote system and no governing table must be preserved.
Use:
<approved classification section>.<local family letter><variant number>

The classification section is the authoritative classification anchor.
The suffix is local project/office syntax, not an official meaning supplied by the classification standard.
The family letter groups related materials within a section.
The number distinguishes documented material variants.

For material-tag and sheet-legend workflows, default to a unique suffix when two variants must appear as separate legend entries. Variants may share a key only when they are intentionally represented by the same legend/specification entry.

A generated keynote is not complete until a matching keynote text-table entry exists and resolves correctly in Revit.

8. AI OUTPUT
AI should return a proposal, not perform an uncontrolled write. The proposal should identify the material, proposed Description, proposed Keynote when applicable, evidence used, and conflicts/uncertainty. These fields may be transient and do not need to be added to the Revit import CSV.

9. COMMIT
CSV workflow:
Revit export -> AI proposal/normalization -> human or rule-based approval -> edit only authorized existing cells -> Revit import.

Bridge workflow:
Read Material -> gather governed evidence -> AI proposal -> preview/dry run -> approved ExternalEvent -> Transaction -> set values -> regenerate/read back -> verify.

10. FAIL SAFE
When evidence is insufficient, omit the unsupported description component or leave the keynote blank. Missing data is preferable to plausible invented BIM data.

notes: Originated from a real ZEN material-governance exercise using an architectural sample material schedule. The project/source identity is intentionally omitted. The key learning was that AI should enrich governed metadata, not free-write it: Description and Keynote serve different documentation purposes, appearance is not specification authority, dimensions should stay out of Description, and a keynote suffix is local unless an authoritative keynote source defines it.
